title: lanq-makeready-fix undo record v1
description: One file per fix session, written by lanq-makeready-fix.ps1 (%ProgramData%\lanq-makeready\fix-<UTC>.json, a folder owned by Administrators that only Administrators and SYSTEM may use) or lanq-makeready-fix.sh (/var/lib/lanq-makeready/fix-<UTC>.json, root only, folder 0700; every fix needs root, so records are written only there). Undo reads only fix-<time>.json files directly in that record folder. Each item is written as pending BEFORE its change and updated after it. The scripts write one item per line in this exact layout, pure ASCII, and reject on undo any file that does not have exactly these fields and shapes. Undo commands are derived from the fix id and the before state; no text from the file is ever run.

os.description: A record is undone only by the script for the same OS.

seq.description: Order the changes were made; undo goes from the highest down. Unique.

id.description: Windows readiness fixes (0.4): ssh.start, ssh.auto, power.sleep, longpaths.on, git.longpaths, ssh.aclkeys. Windows tune fixes (0.5, fix -Tune): power.cpu, power.usbsuspend, startup.vendor, vendor.services, vendor.tasks, sysmain, do.mode, dotnet.env, defender.scantime, defender.exclude. Linux: ssh.start and power.sleep; Linux tune fixes (0.5, fix --tune): sysctl.tune, journald.cap, services.unused, fstrim.timer. Ids are additive: a script that does not know an id rejects the whole record (exit 2).

status.description: pending: written before the change (a crash leaves this); applied: changed and verified; failed: the change or its check failed (after holds what was found); undone: put back and verified; skipped: a pending item whose change was never made (undo found the before state).

before.description: State before the change, in the fixed shape for the id (see stateShapes). Undo restores this.

command.description: The exact command(s) that were run, for people to read. Never executed. The sh script writes at most 510 characters.

after.description: State after the change, same shape as before, or 'unknown'. Undo acts only when the current state equals this ('changed since; left alone' otherwise).

stateShapes.description: Allowed before/after values per fix id. Anything else makes the whole record invalid.

windows:power.sleep.description: The active power scheme (powercfg /getactivescheme, lower case) and its AC timeouts in seconds from powercfg /q; - = unreadable. Undo acts only while the same scheme is active.

windows:longpaths.on.description: HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\FileSystem LongPathsEnabled and its registry type; - = absent. A value of any other type is never changed.

windows:ssh.aclkeys.description: DACL of administrators_authorized_keys in SDDL (allow/deny entries only). A before DACL is also refused on undo unless it has entries, no deny entry, and full control for Administrators and SYSTEM. Undo restores its protection flag and explicit entries; inherited (ID) entries come back from the parent folder.

windows:power.cpu.description: Active power scheme and its AC processor maximum and minimum state in percent (0-100). Undo acts only while the same scheme is active.

windows:power.usbsuspend.description: Active power scheme and its AC USB selective suspend setting.

windows:startup.vendor.description: A Run entry's StartupApproved flag (12 bytes as hex; - = no flag value, which means enabled). sid = the account that ran the fix; an HKCU entry is undone only by that account. HKCU has no Run32. Undo re-checks the name against the curated list and its append-only retired entries.

windows:vendor.services, windows:sysmain.description: The service's Start and DelayedAutostart registry values (0 boot, 1 system, 2 automatic, 3 manual, 4 disabled), restored with sc.exe config start= (delayed-auto when start=2 delayed=1). delayed is compared only when start=2. sysmain: the name is SysMain. Undo re-checks a vendor name against the curated list.

windows:vendor.tasks.description: A scheduled task outside \Microsoft\ (a path under \Microsoft\ is rejected) and whether it is enabled. Undo re-checks the name against the curated list.

windows:do.mode.description: The DODownloadMode policy value under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\DeliveryOptimization; - = absent (the only state the fix starts from).

windows:dotnet.env.description: Machine environment DOTNET_CLI_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT, DOTNET_NOLOGO and DOTNET_GENERATE_ASPNET_CERTIFICATE; - = not set. The fix sets only the unset ones (1, 1, false); undo removes only those.

windows:defender.scantime.description: Defender ScanScheduleDay and the scheduled scan and daily quick scan times in minutes after midnight (0-1439; quick 0 = none).

windows:defender.exclude.description: Whether exactly this folder is in Defender's ExclusionPath list (never '..'). The fix adds work_root or the NuGet packages folder only; undo removes only a path this script added (before excluded=0).

linux:power.sleep.description: systemctl is-enabled of the four sleep targets (none = not found). Undo unmasks only the targets this fix masked.

linux:sysctl.tune.description: fs.inotify.max_user_instances / max_user_watches and whether /etc/sysctl.d/99-zz-lanq-makeready.conf is absent or this script's (first line is its marker). Undo removes the file and sysctl -w puts back only the limits the fix raised.

linux:journald.cap.description: /etc/systemd/journald.conf.d/99-zz-lanq-makeready.conf (SystemMaxUse=1G, RuntimeMaxUse=256M). Undo removes it and restarts journald; journal files deleted by the cap cannot be restored.

linux:services.unused.description: One item per service: svc is a name from the script's APPEND-ONLY list (cups, cups-browsed, bluetooth, modemmanager), and the unit words must match the script's fixed unit table for it (cups: service socket path; the others: service). none = no such unit. Undo re-enables the units that were enabled and starts the ones that were active. Never masks.
